annotation.kind: direct p=2 specialization of equation (4.22) in the proof of Theorem 4.4

assumptions: T0 and T1 are real nonsingular lower-triangular b-by-b diagonal blocks.
The off-diagonal block is represented by the real b-by-r factors X and Y.
The first and second diagonal solves use rounded forward substitution; the off-diagonal action uses the two rounded matrix-vector products from Lemma 3.1; the block subtraction is rounded once.
The standard relative floating-point model excludes overflow and underflow and has valid gamma bounds at dimensions b and r.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P15 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P15 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p15_t2_two_block_equation_4_22 {b r : Nat} (fp : StandardFPModel) (T0 T1 : P15Matrix b) (X Y : P15RectMatrix b r) (v0 v1 : P15Vector b) (hT0diag : forall i, T0 i i != 0) (hT1diag : forall i, T1 i i != 0) (hT0lower : p15LowerTriangular T0) (hT1lower : p15LowerTriangular T1) (hb : GammaValid fp.u b) (hr : GammaValid fp.u r) : let x0 := roundedForwardSub fp b T0 v0; let wInner := p15RoundedRectMatVec fp (p15RectTranspose Y) x0; let wHat := p15RoundedRectMatVec fp X wInner; let rhsHat := fun i => fp.fl_sub (v1 i) (wHat i); let x1 := roundedForwardSub fp b T1 rhsHat; exists DeltaT0 DeltaYT DeltaX theta DeltaT1 DeltaT10, the source Frobenius perturbation bounds and operational equalities hold, the perturbed off-diagonal block is the row-scaled perturbed low-rank product, and the second block row satisfies the p=2 instance of equation (4.22)
formal_statement.plain_language: Prove the p=2 instance of equation (4.22): after the rounded low-rank action, subtraction, and two diagonal solves, the second block row is an exact perturbed block equation with the source's local Frobenius bounds.

informal_proof: Use the forward-substitution backward-error theorem for each diagonal block, equations (3.3)-(3.4) for the low-rank off-diagonal action, and the scalar relative-error model for the single p=2 subtraction. Absorb the subtraction factor into the off-diagonal perturbation and rearrange to obtain equation (4.22).
informal_statement: The direct p=2 specialization of equation (4.22) in the proof of Theorem 4.4, with the rounded operations and local source perturbations exposed.

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The source-faithful p=2 construction needs two distinct substantial results: backward stability of forward substitution and backward stability of a rounded matrix-vector product. Neither is available from Mathlib, and rebuilding both operational inductions dominates the neutral proof.

source_locations.role: selected BLR triangular-solve statement and block algorithm
low-rank block actions, rounded block accumulation, diagonal solves, and gathered perturbation proof

tier_rationale: The p=2 instance of source equation (4.22) requires the distinct substantial NumStability results forwardSub_backward_error and matVec_backward_error. Each replaces a difficult operational finite-precision induction unavailable in Mathlib; Frobenius conversion, one scalar subtraction, and the final rearrangement are simpler support. Together they give L a materially larger advantage than P15-T1.
